{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting / Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review — findings and recommended positions

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The good news is that the clauses that most often trap us are absent or run in our favour: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, non-solicit or liquidated damages obligation on Client; there is no audit right against us; termination for convenience sits with Client alone (notice to the last day of the following month, no exit fee); auto-renewal is annual with a 30-day non-renewal window; and governing law/venue (California, San Luis Obispo County) sits at our fallback.

The exposure is concentrated in risk allocation and exit. Six items are deviations and two are missing:

- **Limitation of liability (medium, deviation).** The only cap is one-sided — TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while Client's liability, including its broad Section 12(a) indemnity, is uncapped. This is expressly walk-away territory and there is no consequential-damages exclusion anywhere in the document.
- **Transition assistance and data return (medium, missing).** No obligation on TrueLink to return Client Content or borrower/loan data, assist migration, or delete and certify deletion; Section 13 instead puts the migration burden on us (30/60 days).
- **Vendor warranty (medium, deviation).** The only warranty is a Y2K date-handling warranty; hosting obligations are "reasonable commercial efforts" only, with no remedy.
- **Vendor indemnity (low, deviation).** TrueLink indemnifies only for its own breach; there is no IP infringement indemnity for the Interface or Services, while Client indemnifies broadly.
- **Insurance (low, missing).** No insurance provision at all, for a vendor that hosts our site and processes our data.
- **IP ownership, licence scope and assignment (low, deviations).** No Client ownership of Support Services work product; the licence does not reach Client affiliates or contractors; and assignment requires unqualified consent with no M&A successor carve-out.

Two minimum-commitment mechanics warrant commercial attention rather than redlining: the Section 5(a) monthly minimums are left blank ($____) and should be set at or below expected usage, and Section 6 excludes those minimums from our supporting-documentation and dispute rights.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity | Vendor capped at 12 months' fees; Client uncapped. No consequential-damages exclusion or Excluded Claims. Make mutual and agreement-wide at greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity (insert at § 14) | No data return, migration assistance or certified deletion. Insert preferred position: 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days, certified deletion. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | **Deviation** | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client | Only a Y2K warranty; no professional-services, conformance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Insert 90-day Services / 12-month software warranty with repair, replacement or refund. Existing disclaimer is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH" and needs no edit. |
| Low | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity | § 12(b) covers TrueLink breach only; no IP infringement indemnity. Insert IP, breach-of-law, TrueLink-caused data breach and wilful misconduct indemnity with standard procedure. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity (insert new § 31) | No insurance requirement anywhere. Insert CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation with certificates; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 2 License | § 2(d) vests Interface ownership in TrueLink; nothing vests Client with the § 4 Support Services work product. Insert Client-ownership/assignment paragraph, licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership. § 8(d) Credit Data bargain left intact. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 License | Grant runs to Client only; no affiliates or contractors, no successor transfer. Add affiliate/contractor coverage on notice and mutual successor carve-out at § 15. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity | § 15 consent is unqualified with only a financially-responsible-affiliate carve-out. Add M&A successor carve-out, reasonableness standard, competitor bar, and confirm Client CoC is not an assignment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 License | Non-exclusive licence; § 2(a) confirms we may acquire, build or license competing products. § 3(i) is a narrow, self-triggered operational term only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 5 Compensation | No penalty or stipulated-sum provision; § 14 exit costs are roughly one month's fees. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 License | No field-of-use restraint; the § 8(d) Non-Competition Agreement reference limits TrueLink. Separate document to be diligenced. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity | Client-only at-will termination, no exit fee. No pro-rata refund language, but billing is monthly in arrears. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation | No audit or inspection right against Client; verification rights run in our favour under §§ 5–6. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 Indemnity | §§ 26–27: California law, exclusive venue San Luis Obispo County. At the fallback; no arbitration or foreign seat. Vendor's home county noted. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 5 Compensation | MFN runs in our favour on Hosting Services rates. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 Compensation | Monthly minimums, but single 12-month term with unconditional exit and no shortfall/take-or-pay. Minimum amounts blank — set commercially. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 7 Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant binding Client. |
| Medium | RENEWAL | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity | § 13: annual auto-renewal, 30 days' non-renewal notice. No renewal reminder or price-increase cap; § 6 partly mitigates. |

## Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (§ 12 / p0077).** The playbook treats "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as walk-away. We require a mutual, agreement-wide cap plus a mutual consequential-damages exclusion before we can sign.
2. **No right to our own hosted data on exit (no transition/data-return clause).** On termination we would have no contractual right to the return of Client Content or borrower/loan data. The finding records this as risking walk-away territory; a data-return and deletion mechanic is a condition of signature.
3. **No insurance from a vendor that processes our data (no insurance clause).** TrueLink hosts our Web Site, holds Client Content and transmits data under the Credit Repository Agreements; the rule's walk-away case is a data-processing vendor carrying no coverage. We need at least the fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the eight open items: mutual liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion; transition assistance, data return and certified deletion at § 14; TrueLink performance and conformance warranty with remedy; TrueLink IP indemnity; new insurance section; Client ownership of Support Services work product with licence-back; affiliate/contractor licence coverage; and the assignment carve-outs and reasonableness standard.
2. **Drafting flag:** the proposed edits for the liability cap and the transition/data-return insertion did not clear automated verification, and the warranty, indemnity, insurance, IP, licence-scope and assignment edits were repaired on review. All eight should be hand-checked against the execution version before the markup goes out.
3. Fill the § 5(a) blanks. Confirm with the business the monthly minimums for Hosting and Support Services and set them at or below expected usage; ask that § 6 documentation and dispute rights extend to the minimums.
4. Obtain and review the separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced at § 8(d) for any personnel or field-of-use restrictions not visible in this document.
5. Confirm we can live with California law and San Luis Obispo County venue (our fallback), or seek a neutral California forum as a low-priority ask.
6. Note for the negotiation record, without redlining: no renewal reminder and no renewal price-increase cap (§ 13, partly mitigated by § 6), and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (immaterial given monthly arrears billing)."}
